metrics.label: Magnificent 7
metrics.description: of S&P 500 is made up of the Mag 7 companies in the S&P 500 - Apple, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Nvidia, Meta, and Tesla. Change refers to the percentage point change from a year ago.
metrics.disclaimer: The Magnificent Seven was coined by Michael Hartnett of Bank of America in 2023 to describe the handful of tech giants driving the market's recovery. Historically, it replaced the FAANG era, reflecting a shift where companies like Nvidia and Microsoft became more influential than former leaders like Netflix. Stock market concentration occurs when these few names represent a disproportionate share of an index, meaning the broader market's health is increasingly tied to the success of just seven firms rather than the hundreds of others.
metrics.dataSource: Calculated from data available at https://www.slickcharts.com/sp500 and https://www.fool.com/research/magnificent-seven-sp-500/.

metrics.label: Corporate Profits
metrics.description: in corporate profits with Inventory Valuation Adjustment (IVA) and Capital Consumption Adjustment (CCAdj) last quarter. Change refers to the percentage change from a year ago.
metrics.disclaimer: Corporate Profits with IVA and CCAdj represents "profits from current production" stripping away the distorting "paper gains" caused by inflation and inconsistent tax accounting. By adjusting for the actual replacement cost of inventory (IVA) and the real-world wear-and-tear of equipment (CCAdj), this metric reveals the true productivity and health of the corporate sector. For the stock market, this serves as a reality check: while reported earnings-per-share can be inflated by stock buybacks or accounting tricks, this adjusted figure tracks the fundamental ability of firms to generate value. When these "economic" profits stagnate while stock prices continue to climb, it often signals that the market is overextended and overdue for a correction.
metrics.dataSource: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, Corporate Profits with Inventory Valuation Adjustment (IVA) and Capital Consumption Adjustment (CCAdj) [CPROFIT], retrieved from FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis; https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CPROFIT.
